ai.title: Fix agent publishing with undefined system prompts
ai.summary: Agent publishing now handles undefined system prompts by defaulting them to empty strings in `validateSingleAgent`. The `validateAgents` function returns `dynamicTemplates` to preserve validated configs. Publish requests use loose `z.record` schemas, with strict validation moved to `validateAgents` in the web API route. CLI matching logic simplified to ignore template keys.

eli5.text: When someone tried to publish an agent (a pre-built assistant) that was missing its instructions, the whole publishing process used to fail, blocking the upload even if everything else was fine. Now the publishing system treats a missing instruction field as empty instead of breaking, so an agent without that set value can still be published. If you tried to publish an agent before, a blank or undefined instruction box could have silently stopped it; now it just goes through.

ai.summary: Deleted PLACEHOLDER constants and types from agent-definition.ts. Updated tool call docs to use input instead of args. Made WebSearchParams.depth optional in tools.ts.

eli5.text: The system has removed placeholder text templates that were used as temporary stand-ins for dynamic content in agent definitions. This affects developers who configure or extend the agent tooling, since those placeholder constants (like AGENT_NAME, AGENTS_PROMPT, CONFIG_SCHEMA, etc.) are no longer available for use in agent definition files. If you looked at the agent definition templates today, you would no longer find the PLACEHOLDER object or its associated types and values; instead, documentation now refers to tool calls using 'input' rather than 'args', and WebSearchParams.depth is now optional. This is a behind-the-scenes cleanup that simplifies how agent templates are defined, with no direct impact visible to end users of the agents themselves.

ai.title: Update GPT-5 base prompts
ai.summary: Revised GPT-5 conditional prompt strings in `.agents/prompts/base-prompts.ts`. Replaced specific 'chain tools' instructions with broader 'Proactive Execution' and 'comprehensive tool usage' directives. Adjusted `end_turn` semantics to emphasize feedback signaling over termination.

eli5.text: When the assistant works on GPT-5, it now tries harder to just get things done instead of stopping to check in, using whatever tools it needs, reading files, searching code, even spinning off helper agents, to finish the whole task before handing control back. It also treats the end-of-turn signal as a way to say 'I need your input here' rather than just quitting, so it keeps working autonomously unless it's truly blocked or wants your review.

ai.title: Add local package.json for isolated agents workspace
ai.summary: Introduced `.agents/package.json` to define the `@codebuff/agents` package, establishing an isolated workspace for agent-related code. This change excludes the root `tsconfig.base.json`, allowing independent configuration and typechecking via a local `bun x tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` script. The new file sets the module type to ESM and marks the package as private, ensuring it remains internal to the repository structure.

eli5.text: The team added a small configuration file inside a folder that holds the assistant's agent code, which tells the system how to build and check that specific folder on its own instead of relying on the main project setup. This means the agent code can now be tested and type-checked independently using its own settings. If you were to open that folder, you'd see a new file listing basic project details and a command that runs the type-checking tool locally.

Instead of writing helper rules in a basic text format, you can now write them using a more powerful programming language, and the guidance shows you how to add fields that tell other helpers when it's useful to call on this helper, how its results should be structured, and how to control the helper's behavior step-by-step with code.

ai.title: agents-typecheck script routes through .agents typecheck
ai.summary: The `agents-typecheck` command in `codebuff.json` now invokes `bun run typecheck` with `cwd` set to `.agents`, replacing the direct `bun x tsc --noEmit -p .agents/tsconfig.json` call. This change aligns the agent type-checking script with the local `package.json` configuration in the `.agents` directory, ensuring consistent tooling and dependency resolution. The modification is scoped to `codebuff.json` and does not affect user-facing CLI or Web surfaces.

eli5.text: The assistant's internal type-checking process was re-routed through a different configuration file. Previously, it ran a direct check using a specific tool path. Now, it delegates to a standard script located in a subdirectory. This ensures the checking uses the same settings and dependencies that are already defined there. It only affects how the system validates its own code, and there is no change to anything you would see or interact with.

ai.summary: Changed HTTP method from POST to GET in `validateAgentDefinitionsIfAuthenticated`. The request still sends `JSON.stringify({ agentDefinitions })` in the `body`. Affects `npm-app/src/utils/agent-validation.ts`. Sending a body with GET is non-standard and may be stripped by some HTTP clients or proxies.

eli5.text: The system now asks a server for agent validation using a GET request instead of a POST request, even though it still sends data in the request body. This is non-standard and may cause some servers or proxies to ignore the data. Only internal tools and developers working on agent validation will notice this change. It is a minor, behind-the-scenes adjustment with no direct impact on end users.

ai.title: SDK auto-parses knowledgeFiles from projectFiles
ai.summary: The SDK `initialSessionState` function now automatically populates `knowledgeFiles` by filtering `projectFiles` for paths ending in `knowledge.md` or `claude.md` if `knowledgeFiles` is undefined. This change simplifies initialization by removing the need to manually extract these specific files. The behavior is scoped to `sdk/src/run-state.ts` and documented in `sdk/CHANGELOG.md`. Note that existing explicit `knowledgeFiles` inputs remain unaffected, ensuring backward compatibility.

eli5.text: When a developer sets up a new session using this software kit, they no longer have to manually point it at instruction files named knowledge.md or claude.md sitting alongside their project files. The kit now scans all the files they provide and automatically pulls out any whose names end with knowledge.md or claude.md, treating those as the knowledge files to load. This only happens if they didn't already specify which knowledge files to use, so anything they set explicitly stays exactly the same. The change is live today in the kit's latest version.

ai.title: Fix SDK maxAgentSteps reset
ai.summary: SDK `CodebuffClient` now explicitly sets `sessionState.mainAgentState.stepsRemaining` to the resolved `maxAgentSteps` value, preventing the agent step counter from resetting every run. Introduced `DEFAULT_MAX_AGENT_STEPS` constant in `common/src/json-config/constants.ts` to replace the hardcoded default in `CodebuffConfigSchema`. Applied to `sdk/src/client.ts` and `common/src/json-config/constants.ts`.

eli5.text: When you ask the coding assistant to work on your project, it can now keep track of how many steps it has left to take without resetting that count at the start of each run, so longer tasks don't get cut off unexpectedly. The default limit is now set through a shared configuration value instead of being hardcoded in one place. If you looked, you would see that previously the step counter restarted from the maximum on every new attempt, whereas now it continues from where it left off. This affects anyone using the software development kit to build tools that run the assistant programmatically.

ai.title: Clarify context-manager vs specialty agents
ai.summary: Documentation in `web/src/content/agents/customizing-agents.mdx` clarifies the distinction between context-manager agents and specialty reviewer agents. Adds a comparison table, a design checklist for shaping agents around task breakdown and context control, and usage tips for spawning reviewers.

eli5.text: The guide for building custom AI assistants now clearly separates two roles: a coordinator assistant that plans work and hands off pieces to specialized reviewer assistants, versus single-purpose reviewer assistants that zoom in on specific checks. You'd notice this in the written guidance itself, not in any live behavior, since it's just documentation, but if you build assistants from it, you'll follow a checklist that walks you through defining the end goal, breaking work into phases, deciding what to spawn versus handle inline, and capturing checkpoints so work can resume. The tips tell coordinator assistants to call reviewer assistants at the right moment in the workflow rather than trying to make one assistant do everything.

This only affects the agent-template schema views in the docs; the shorter config-schema display is unchanged and still renders in full.
